question.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square for the expression inside the square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+10x+24 & ={x}^{2}+10x+({5}^{2}-{5}^{2})+24 \\  & =({x}^{2}+10x+25)-25+24 \\  & =(x+5)^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
{\int }_{\sqrt{2}-5}^{-3}\frac{60}{|x+5|\sqrt{{x}^{2}+10x+24}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{\sqrt{2}-5}^{-3}\frac{60}{|x+5|\sqrt{(x+5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This resembles the basic integral for inverse secant:

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}\,u+C
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $x+5.$

So, let's perform the substitution

$$
u=x+5.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Let's use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $\sqrt{2}-5$ | $-3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $2$ |

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\sqrt{2}-5}^{-3}\frac{60}{|x+5|\sqrt{{x}^{2}+10x+24}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}-5}^{-3}\frac{60}{|x+5|\sqrt{(x+5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}\frac{60}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =60\text{arcsec }u\,{|}_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} \\  & =60(\text{arcsec}(2)-\text{arcsec}(\sqrt{2})) \\  & =60(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =5\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
